name: Zayn al-Dīn Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr al-Jirjāwī al-Azharī
summary: The lamp-lighter of al-Azhar who became its grammarian: author of al-Taṣrīḥ on Ibn Hishām's Awḍaḥ al-masālik, a commentary on al-Ājurrūmiyya and the beginners' books of iʿrāb.
bio: Khālid was born in Jirjā in Upper Egypt in 838/1434 and grew up in Cairo. The biographers tell that he served as a lamp-lighter in al-Azhar, and that one night a wick fell from his hand onto a student's notes; the student called him ignorant, and he set himself to learn, beginning, by these reports, at thirty-six. He became one of the best-known teachers of grammar of the mosque, and died on his way back from the pilgrimage in 905/1499.

His al-Taṣrīḥ bi-maḍmūn al-Tawḍīḥ comments on Ibn Hishām's Awḍaḥ al-masālik, itself a commentary on the Alfiyya, and became a standard book of the Azhar. For beginners he wrote a commentary on al-Ājurrūmiyya, al-Muqaddima al-Azhariyya with its commentary, Mūṣil al-ṭullāb on Ibn Hishām's rules of iʿrāb, and Tamrīn al-ṭullāb, the iʿrāb of the Alfiyya verse by verse.
uncertain: The age at which he began to study is given only by later biographers.
